      About the content

      This manual covers every part of Car & Engine simulator, a Blender add-on that turns any car model into a car you can drive in the viewport, with vehicle physics underneath and an engine sound built from the simulation's own rpm. There is one chapter for each area of the Car Sim tab.

      It needs Blender 4.2 or newer, and the four wheels of your car model must be separate objects from the body.

      Warnings and symbols

      Different types of notices and symbols are used in the descriptions.

      WARNING

      Blender may freeze or crash

      Failure to follow notices in the "Warning" category may freeze Blender or lose unsaved work.

      CAUTION

      Blender may slow down

      Failure to follow notices in the "Caution" category may make the viewport or rendering noticeably slower.

      NOTE

      Unexpected result possible

      Failure to follow notices in the "Note" category may give a result you did not expect — for example a render with no sound.

      INFORMATION

      Useful background, tips and limits worth knowing.

      Instructions and text

      • Bold names are buttons, settings and panels exactly as they appear in Blender.
      • Italic paths such as Preferences → Add-ons tell you where to click.
      • Keys are the default key bindings.
      • Panels drawn from the add-on respond like Blender's, shown with an Audi RS7 loaded: drag or click a number, tick a box, open a menu or fold a panel. Nothing you change is kept.

      An instruction that you carry out.

      1. Steps that you carry out in this order.

      Fig. 1 numbers the pictures in each chapter.

      Getting started

      The add-on installs as a Blender extension. Everything it does is in the Car Sim tab of the 3D view sidebar (press N).

      Settings that apply to every file — key bindings, the controller, the acceleration timer and the experimental switch — are in Preferences → Add-ons → Car Simulator + sound.

      Build a rig

      1. Open or import your car. Any model works, as long as the four wheels are separate objects from the body.
      2. Detect Car Parts. Finds the wheels and body and reports the wheelbase, track and tire radii. Assign anything it missed in the Parts list, or use Auto-Assign with a name to match.
      3. Build Rig. Creates the hubs, steering, suspension, collision shapes and sound emitters. Everything is named CARSIM_* and kept in its own collection.
      4. Drive (Live). The viewport becomes the car. Press Esc to stop.

      Proxy Detail sets how closely the body collision shape follows the bodywork (see Ground & collisions). The sound emitters are created selected — move them to the engine bay and the tailpipe.

      After the build

      Check that the hubs sit at the wheel centres. A car that pulls to one side on a straight almost always has a hub slightly out of place — fix it with Hub Center under Tires & Brakes.

      WARNING

      Blender can freeze on some graphics drivers.

      This is a driver problem, not an add-on one.

      Press Win + Ctrl + Shift + B to reset the display driver.

      Set the graphics backend to Vulkan in Preferences → System and restart Blender.

      Remove a rig

      • Keep My Settings — deletes only the rig objects. Sound emitters, smoke setup, tire-mark material and all panel settings stay, ready for the next rig.
      • Clear Everything — removes all of it.
      INFORMATION

      Detecting parts and building the rig never move your model and never change Ground Z. If the car sits above or below the ground, the add-on tells you instead of moving anything.

      Controls

      Defaults are shown below. All keys can be changed in Preferences → Add-ons → Car Simulator + sound → Keyboard Controls.

      KeyAction
      W SThrottle / brake
      A DSteer left / right
      SpaceHandbrake
      Q EGear down / up
      TabAutomatic gearbox on / off
      Shift + P R N DPark, reverse, neutral, drive
      Alt + Shift + SStart / stop the engine
      CCycle camera — chase, fixed, hood, interior
      LLights — off, running, low beam, high beam
      ↑ ↓Lights up / down through the same four
      , . or ← →Left / right indicator
      Both indicators, or hold oneHazards
      BHorn (hold)
      K JSet cruise / resume
      = -Cruise speed up / down
      GStart or restart a race
      H IHUD / cluster style
      RReset the car
      EscStop driving
      INFORMATION

      Launch control

      Hold throttle and brake together at a standstill to arm it.

      Release the brake to launch.

      Controller

      A PS5 DualSense controller works over USB or Bluetooth and is picked up automatically. The button map is in Controller Controls (PS5 DualSense) in the add-on preferences.

      The car

      Every panel in this chapter is per car. With several cars in a scene, the panels show whichever car is active in the Garage.

      Presets

      108 cars ship with the add-on — 68 rear-drive, 37 all-wheel drive and 3 front-drive. A preset sets engine, gearing, weight, aero and suspension together. Match Tone To Vehicle then points the engine sound at the same figures.

      Mass and balance

      Mass, Front Weight, CG Height and Unsprung Mass decide most of how the car behaves.

      Fuel Load is off by default. Give it a load to model the tank: Tank Size, Tank Position, and Burn Fuel, which empties the tank as you drive and shifts the balance.

      Engine and aero

      Peak power and torque with their rpm, redline, idle and Engine Inertia (how fast the engine revs up). Speed Limiter caps top speed. Drag CdA and front/rear Downforce (at 30 m/s) set the aero.

      Engine management

      Induction
      Naturally aspirated, turbocharged or supercharged. Peak Boost and Spool set boost and lag.
      Estimate Engine
      Works out capacity, cylinders, VE and injector size from your power and torque figures. The quickest way to a car that runs.
      Fuelling and Map
      Closed-loop fuelling with trim authority, injector flow and dead time. Generate Base Map fills the VE and air/fuel tables; Show Table displays them.
      Shifting
      Automatic modes (Normal, Sport, Eco), shift points, shift time and torque cut. The line above the sliders shows the actual rpm each shift point works out to.

      Drivetrain

      Layout (front, rear or all-wheel drive with a front split), limited-slip diff, gearbox and final drive. Automatics add a torque converter, idle creep and a parking pawl. The rolling radius shown at the bottom comes from the rig.

      Suspension & steering

      Architecture

      Choose front and rear separately from six layouts — MacPherson strut, double wishbone, five-link, semi-trailing arm, twist beam and live axle — on coil, air or hydropneumatic springs. Air springs add a pressure and levelling rate; a front and rear payload loads the car up.

      Roll centres

      With Roll Centres From Linkage on, roll-centre heights, jacking and weight transfer come from the linkage. Turn it off to set the heights yourself. Roll Centre Migration is how much they move as the car rolls.

      Springs and dampers

      Spring rates, damping ratio, anti-roll bars, and bump and droop travel. The Suspension preset (Comfort, Sport and so on) sets them all at once; Comfort Firmness leans it either way.

      Tire enveloping

      Contact Patch, Carcass Wrap and Tire Stiffness let the tire wrap over a kerb instead of hitting it like a solid wheel.

      Steering

      Max Steer / Drift Lock
      Normal lock, and the lock Drift Setup switches to.
      Steer Speed / Steer Return
      How fast the wheel turns and self-centres. Steer Speed gives the same road-wheel rate under every Speed Law, so the wheel arrives when asked at any speed.
      Ackermann / Caster Feedback
      Steering geometry and self-aligning feel.
      Speed Law
      How lock is scaled with speed, so the same input doesn't ask for the same angle at 20 mph and 120. Parking-speed steering stays full under every law.
      Steering Axis
      Kingpin inclination, caster and scrub radius — read from the linkage by default. The line underneath shows what is in force.

      Toe, camber and ride height, front and rear, update live while you drive.

      INFORMATION

      Camber and grip

      Camber Affects Grip is off by default: camber makes side force but costs no grip, which is forgiving. Turn it on and a badly cambered wheel loses grip like a real one.

      Show Suspension draws the linkage in the viewport. Rebuild Suspension remakes the parts after you change the architecture.

      Driver aids & ignition

      Assists

      ABS, traction control, stability control, launch control, cruise control and a rev limiter. Each is modelled, not faked, and each can be switched off. ESC Strength sets how hard stability control steps in.

      INFORMATION

      The assists stop a drift.

      Traction and stability control stop a slide before it starts — with them on, no rear-drive car gets past about 7° of slip.

      Turn them off, or press Drift Setup. It turns them off and adds more lock, quicker steering, a locked-feeling diff and stiffer rear bars.

      Cruise control

      K sets and cancels, = and - adjust, J resumes. Braking, the handbrake or leaving Drive cancels it. It won't engage below its minimum speed.

      Ignition

      Start and stop the engine with Alt + Shift + S. Engagement Inhibit refuses a gear above a set rpm. The other settings shape the start: crank time and rpm, the flare as it catches, the fast idle afterwards, and the run-down when switched off. Battery and Condition let a tired car struggle to start.

      Rev limiter and launch control

      The rev limiter has a soft and a hard style and works in Park and Neutral only — in gear, the road sets the revs.

      Launch control arms when you hold throttle and brake at a standstill, and launches when you release the brake.

      Launch RPM
      Where it holds the engine.
      Launch Slip Target
      How much wheelspin it allows.
      Launch Squat
      How much the car sits down.
      Launch Exit Speed
      Where it hands control back to you.

      Lights

      Press Set Up Light Materials. It finds the emissive materials on the car and wires each one to the right lamp, so the lights use the materials your model already has.

      Levels and timing

      A brightness for each function — running, brake, DRL, headlight, reverse and indicator — plus flash rate and rise/fall times, so a filament lamp glows up and fades rather than snapping. Indicator colour is set as a temperature, front and rear separately. Low and high beams are set in watts.

      The indicator colour looks the same whether a lamp's material uses a Blackbody node or a plain colour.

      Sequential sweep

      Modern indicators fill from the inside out. Sweep Time is how long the fill takes, Sweep Edge how soft the moving edge is. Welcome Sweep plays it once when the car is unlocked. Measure Sweep Axes works out which way each lamp sweeps; a centre lamp opens from the middle out.

      Lamp groups

      Headlights, tail lights, separate indicators, low beam, high beam and reverse. Each group can double as an indicator, be sequential, and join in on hazards. Sweep ready means the axes are measured and the sweep will run.

      INFORMATION

      If two lamp materials share a node group, the add-on gives each its own copy when a drive starts, so left and right indicators can flash independently.

      INFORMATION

      While driving

      ↑ ↓ step through off, DRL, low and high. ← → are the indicators; press both, or hold one for about a second, for hazards. L and , . do the same.

      Tire smoke & tire marks

      Tire smoke

      Smoke follows tread temperature, not slip directly — so a long slide smokes harder at the end than the start.

      Heat
      Heat Buildup and Cooling set how fast the tread heats and cools. Smoke Point is where smoke starts, Onset Width how sharply, and Afterglow how long it lasts once you're off it.
      Emission
      Density, spread around the contact patch, how much the car carries along, randomness and buoyancy. Smoke settles on the road surface instead of sinking into it.
      Wheel Flow
      Adds the air the wheel moves — a jet off the contact patch and a vortex around the wheel — so smoke rolls like it does behind a real car.
      Colliders and Domain
      Colliders wire the tires (and optionally the body) into the smoke domain so the plume breaks around them. Domain holds resolution, dissolve time and vorticity.

      Record Tire Smoke keys the emission with the take, so a replay smokes where the drive did. Readouts marked as guessed settle once a take has been driven.

      Tire marks

      Every simulated car lays its own marks, so a race leaves the whole field's lines on the road.

      The mark
      Darkness, Onset (slip needed before it shows), Detail, Width, Tail Fade, lift off the road, and how overlaps combine. Burnout Rate, Heat Response and ABS Chatter add marks from burnouts, hot tires and pulsing ABS.
      Look
      The surface (asphalt, concrete…) and everything that makes rubber read as rubber: opacity, edge softness, profile, striations, break-up, roughness, sheen and relief. Refresh Look rebuilds the material after a change.
      • Clear On Record — wipes the road when a take starts.
      • Join Tire Marks — merges the marks into one object.
      • Clear Tire Marks — removes them all.

      Engine sound

      The engine is synthesised from the simulation's own rpm, load and throttle — there are no samples. Live Sound is what you hear while driving.

      Presets
      Whole voices to start from, and where your own are saved.
      Engine
      Layout, cylinder count, firing order and the spread that gives a V8 its lope and a flat-six its wail.
      Engine Braking
      What it sounds like off the throttle.
      Forced Induction
      Turbo or supercharger whine, spool, blow-off and flutter.
      Exhaust
      Pipe length, resonance and overrun. Active Exhaust Valve opens a bypass under load, like a modern car.
      Mix
      Levels of every layer: engine, exhaust, starter, tire screech, rolling noise and the drive-by whoosh.
      Distance Falloff
      How the car quietens with distance from the camera, and the Doppler as it passes.

      Match Tone To Vehicle (in the Vehicle panel) points the sound at the car's capacity, cylinders and redline — the fastest way to a sound that fits.

      Turbo flutter

      Lift off at boost with no blow-off valve and the turbo flutters — "stu-tu-tu". It also fires on every upshift under power. Release, under Forced Induction, sets its character: 0 is a soft, voiced "tu"; 1 is a sharper burst of air. Default is 0.65.

      Overrun pops

      Pops and crackles on a lift, densest right after you lift and tapering off. Pops sometimes come in short runs, an upshift under power gives a "brap", and pops follow the Doppler like the rest of the car.

      The settings are under Exhaust:

      Pops Per Second
      How busy the crackle is.
      Pop Duration
      How long the pops go on after a lift.
      Bang Size
      How big the pops are.

      Overrun pops are an experimental feature.

      Cylinder on Demand

      A V8 cruises as a four at light load and switches back to all cylinders as soon as you press past about 30% throttle. An experimental feature.

      NOTE

      A render is silent without a bake.

      Blender's renderer can't hear the live engine.

      Bake the audio before rendering — see Recording & rendering.

      Ground & collisions

      Ground Z is the height of the road. It stays where you set it — building a rig never moves it.

      Ground type

      • Flat Plane — an infinite level surface at Ground Z. Fast, and right for most shots.
      • Mesh Terrain — the car follows hills, ramps and banking, and can leave the ground. Any mesh in the collider collection works, high or low poly.

      With Solid Colliders on, the body and wheels hit walls, kerbs, tunnel roofs and anything else with faces.

      INFORMATION

      Limits

      Loops and anything that takes the car past vertical are not supported. Colliders that deform without moving (armature, shape keys, geometry nodes) are read once when the drive starts — animated changes after that aren't seen.

      Body proxy detail

      Proxy Detail sets how closely the collision shape follows the bodywork, and so how much gap is left when two cars touch. Higher is tighter but costs more bake time and a little per step. Drop it on a big field; raise it if cars stop with a visible gap. The readout under Build Body Proxy shows the numbers.

      Deformation

      Experimental — turn it on in the add-on preferences and it appears under Colliders.

      Dent The Bodywork
      Impacts crumple the car where it was hit, in the direction it was hit, scaled by mass — the hatchback that hits the van is the one that bends. Damage builds up over a drive. Straighten Panels or Reset clears it. Recorded takes key the damage on the frame it happened, and the bent body is kept for rendering.
      Squash The Tires
      Flattens the contact patch and bulges the sidewall under load; softer tires deflect more. Squash Limit is the rim. Squash Reach is how far up the wheel the flattening goes — lower it if the rim starts to move, raise it for a tall sidewall. Squash is recorded with the take.
      CAUTION

      Deformation can slow Blender down.

      A deforming modifier makes Blender re-evaluate the mesh every frame. An undamaged car carries none; one is added on the first dent and removed by Straighten Panels. Tire squash changes every frame, so expect a few milliseconds per wheel on a heavy wheel mesh (around 250k vertices).

      INFORMATION

      Deformation is cosmetic. The car keeps colliding as its undamaged shape, so handling is unaffected. It's a smooth crumple, not torn panels or sharp creases, and it needs a body proxy.

      Cars hitting each other

      Cars Hit Each Other makes the cars in the scene solid to one another. It's on by default and works on both ground types. See Multiple cars.

      Paths & autopilot

      Point Follow Path at a curve and the car plans the whole line up front: it brakes before a corner rather than in it, and if it can't make a corner it goes slower there for the rest of the lap. The settings are at the bottom of the Driver Aids panel.

      NOTE

      A mesh path gives a rough drive.

      Curves are sampled every 0.5 m; a mesh is read vertex by vertex, so a coarse mesh gives a coarse road.

      Use a Curve object, not a mesh.

      If you have already converted it to a mesh, subdivide it.

      Settings

      Speed Limit
      Top speed on a straight. Corners set their own speed.
      Pace
      How hard the driver uses the tires. 1.0 is the limit; above it asks for grip the car doesn't have.
      Look Ahead
      How far down the road it aims. Higher cuts corners more.
      Line Offset
      Drive to one side of the line — for a second car on the same path.
      Reverse Direction
      Drive the curve the other way.
      At The End
      Stop, keep driving, return, or loop.

      Road width

      By default the car drives the exact line you drew. Set a Road Width and the path becomes the middle of a road — calmer, and far smoother on a hand-drawn curve. Use The Road lets it take a racing line (out wide, apex, out again). It only gains time on a wide road, so it's off by default.

      Drift

      The Drift slider lets the car drift through corners on a path — 0 grips, 1 slides as much as it can.

      • Very powerful cars can spin at middle Drift settings. Try Drift at 1.0.
      • Very grippy cars may not break loose at all.
      • Raising Pace does not help it drift.

      Path Assist

      For shots where the car must go exactly where you told it rather than where the physics allows. At 0 the tires decide everything. Turn it up and the car's position, heading and slide are eased toward the line; at 1 it's on rails and never misses a corner.

      • Engine, gearbox, suspension, wheels, sound and lights all behave normally at every setting.
      • A real impact drops the assist for about 1.5 seconds, then the car drives itself back onto the line.
      • In a race it applies to the whole field — nobody spins or runs wide, so order is decided by pace. Cars still avoid each other.

      Path Assist is in Driver Aids, on each Garage slot and in the race settings, next to Drift.

      INFORMATION

      The path follower works in 2D. With a Flat Plane ground, a path with height in it is driven at Ground Z. For a road that climbs, use Mesh Terrain with a real road surface.

      Avoiding obstacles

      With Obstacle sensing on (an experimental feature), a car on a path steers around something in its way and holds the swerve until it's past.

      Multiple cars

      Garage → Cars In This Scene lists every car in the file. Each keeps its own settings, engine, camera and mounts.

      • Make Active — take control of a car.
      • Store — save its current state.
      • Reset All — put the whole field back to the start, or to before the last drive.
      • Take Over — switch cars, even mid-drive. The car you leave carries on under its own driver.

      What the other cars do

      Parked
      Sits on its springs and reacts when hit. Can have its engine running.
      Follow A Path
      Driven round a curve by the autopilot.
      Follow The Active Car
      Holds station on you — behind, behind-left/right, alongside, or in front, at a set gap.
      Not Simulated
      Stays exactly where it is. Costs nothing, but can't be hit. Use Parked for an obstacle you want to shunt.

      Four switches set how much the field joins in: Simulate Other Cars, Record Them Too, They Lay Rubber Too and They Make Noise Too. Markers float a coloured tag over each car; click one to switch to it.

      Contact between cars

      Cars are solid to each other. A shunt pushes the car ahead; a rub scrubs speed off both. Heavier cars move lighter ones more. A car needs a body proxy to be hit. Turn it off with Cars Hit Each Other (Ground & collisions) for a ghost lap or a camera car.

      INFORMATION

      Cars following you

      A gap of 10–15 m and a Pace around 0.85 gives the calmest result.

      INFORMATION

      Float Origin is paused while more than one car is on track. On a very long drive with a field, precision drifts slightly.

      Recording & rendering

      Record a take

      Switch Record on before you drive. The drive is saved as keyframes: position, wheels, suspension, lights, camera and lens, plus rpm, gear, throttle, brake, speed and slip. Tire smoke and deformation are keyed too. Takes are filed, so you can keep several and switch between them.

      A take is ordinary Blender animation — edit, retime or layer it. The add-on doesn't need to be running to play it back.

      Bake the audio

      The renderer can't hear the live engine, so bake it for any render with sound.

      1. Drive with Record on.
      2. Press Engine Sound → Bake Audio For Render. Every recorded car is baked from its own engine settings, to its own file, on its own sequencer channel.
      3. Render to a movie format with an audio codec selected.
      INFORMATION

      The bake uses the throttle, brake and rpm you actually recorded, so it sounds like what you heard, with tire screech, starter, rolling noise and Doppler at the Mix levels.

      Set Sample Rate to match Output → Audio. The panel warns you if they differ.

      The Garage

      The browser at the top is your library of saved cars, shown as previews, a grid or a list. Spawn Vehicle drops the selected car into the scene, ready to drive, at the 3D cursor or wherever you choose.

      • Save As New Preset — saves the whole car (geometry references, tuning, ECU tables, engine tone, lights, camera mounts) with a thumbnail.
      • Update — overwrites the preset the car came from. Greyed out for a spawned car; save it as new instead.

      Presets live in a folder you choose, so you can move, share and back them up like any other asset. Cars In This Scene is covered in Multiple cars.

      Experimental features

      Some newer and heavier features ship switched off. Turn them on with Experimental Features in Preferences → Add-ons → Car Simulator + sound. Until then they are hidden and inactive — a file saved with one enabled won't run it on a machine where the switch is off.

      • Race mode
      • Slipstream
      • Obstacle sensing
      • Body and tire deformation
      • Overrun pops
      • Tire roar
      • Cylinder on demand
      • The engine fault lamp
      • Modifier suspension

      Troubleshooting

      Blender froze, or the viewport went black

      Press Win + Ctrl + Shift + B to reset the display driver. Then set the graphics backend to Vulkan in Preferences → System and restart Blender.

      Detect Car Parts can't find my wheels

      The wheels must be separate objects. If they're joined to the body, separate them (P → By Loose Parts in Edit Mode). Or assign them in the Parts list, or use Auto-Assign.

      The car pulls to one side on a straight

      A hub isn't quite at the wheel centre. Adjust Hub Center under Tires & Brakes.

      The car sits above or below the ground

      Ground Z defaults to zero and doesn't move. Move the model to the floor, or set Ground Z to match — the rig report tells you how far off it is.

      The car won't slide

      Traction and stability control are on by default. Switch them off, or press Drift Setup.

      A car on a path won't drift, or spins

      Check the Drift slider. Very powerful cars can spin at middle settings — try 1.0. Very grippy cars may not break loose at all.

      The engine won't start

      Press Alt + Shift + S. If it cranks but doesn't catch, check Battery and Condition under Ignition.

      A car following a path drives erratically

      Usually a coarse mesh path — use a Curve, or subdivide the mesh. Otherwise drop Pace to about 0.85 and Look Ahead to 1.0. If it must hold the line exactly, raise Path Assist.

      My render has no sound

      Drive with Record on, press Bake Audio For Render, and render to a movie format with an audio codec. The bake places the sound strips and turns the sequencer on for you.

      The engine sounds thin or wrong for the car

      Check layout and cylinder count in Engine Sound → Engine, and that the redline matches. Use Match Tone To Vehicle.

      Baked audio is louder or quieter than live

      Both use the Mix levels. If one car is much louder than the rest, check Distance Falloff and where that car's sound emitters are.

      The lights do nothing

      Press Set Up Light Materials first. For a sequential sweep, a group needs the Sweep ready tick — press Measure Sweep Axes.

      No tire smoke, or it comes from the wrong place

      Check the emitters are in place — the panel shows how many it found. A short slip may not reach the smoke point; lower it or raise Heat Buildup. For readouts marked guessed, record a take and press Rebuild Wheel Flow.

      An experimental feature is missing

      Turn on Experimental Features in the add-on preferences.

      Driving stutters

      The physics isn't affected by a slow viewport, but it's harder to drive. Hide what you don't need, use solid shading, or turn on the experimental modifier suspension.

      The controller does nothing

      Connect it before starting a drive and check Preferences → Controller Controls. It must be in DualSense mode, not an emulation mode set by other software.
